title: Property Inheritance in Bangladesh for NRBs: Muslim, Hindu and Christian Law
metaTitle: Property Inheritance in Bangladesh for NRBs: Muslim, Hindu, Christian
metaDescription: How inheritance works in Bangladesh for people living abroad: Muslim law shares, Hindu Dayabhaga and Christian succession, heirship certificate, mutation and how to protect your share.
heroIntro: When a parent dies in Bangladesh, the children abroad often hear that "everything is already settled" and discover years later that their share was sold, transferred by a forged deed or occupied by one sibling. Knowing how inheritance works, and acting early, is the best protection. This guide is written by Advocate Md. Shah Alam, Supreme Court of Bangladesh, for Bangladeshis living in the UK, USA, UAE, Canada and elsewhere. For case-specific help you can call the chamber on 01712655546 or WhatsApp the same number.

quickAnswer.heading: Inheritance in Bangladesh: Key Points
points: Inheritance follows the personal law of the deceased: Muslim law, Hindu (Dayabhaga) law or the Succession Act 1925 for Christians.
Under Muslim law, shares are fixed: for example a daughter gets half the share of a son, and a widow gets 1/8 with children and 1/4 without.
All heirs, including those abroad, have a right to their share even if they never live in the property.
Get an heirship certificate (Warish Sanad), then apply for mutation in the names of all heirs.
If heirs cannot agree, a partition suit can be filed in the Civil Court.

sections.content:
Bangladesh has no single inheritance statute for everyone. The religion of the deceased decides which law applies:

  • Muslims: Muslim personal law (Sharia, mainly Hanafi), supplemented by the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance 1961 (for example, the rights of orphaned grandchildren).
  • Hindus: Dayabhaga school (mostly in Bangladesh), with the Hindu Women's Right to Property Act 1937.
  • Christians and others: the Succession Act 1925.

A will can also change the picture, but a Muslim can leave only up to one-third of the estate by will to a non-heir without the consent of the other heirs.

This article is general legal information, not legal advice. Fees, forms and procedures change; confirm current requirements with the relevant office or a qualified advocate before acting.

Muslim law fixes the shares of the main heirs. The exact result depends on who survives the deceased, and you should always have your advocate calculate it, but the following are the commonly applied rules:

  • Wife: 1/8 if there are children, 1/4 if there are no children (shared among wives).
  • Husband: 1/4 if there are children, 1/2 if there are none.
  • Sons and daughters: the residue after fixed shares, with each son receiving twice a daughter's share.
  • Only daughter: 1/2; two or more daughters (no sons): 2/3 together.
  • Mother: 1/6 if there are children, otherwise 1/3.
  • Father: 1/6 if there are children plus residue in some cases.

Heirs living abroad have exactly the same rights as heirs who live in Bangladesh. Debts, funeral expenses and valid bequests are paid first.

Under the Dayabhaga system, the sons, widow and daughters inherit on the death of the owner. In general, sons take the property equally; a widow can inherit a share equal to a son in the absence of other heirs and holds a limited interest; and a daughter inherits mainly in the absence of sons or widow. The rules are complex, and recent reform proposals are not yet complete, so get advice for your specific family.

Under the Succession Act 1925, if a Christian dies without a will, the spouse and children take specified shares: one-third to the widow and two-thirds to the children, equally (if there is no child, shares go to other kin). If there is a valid will, probate or letters of administration are obtained from the District Judge.

1. Obtain the death certificate of the deceased.
  2. Get the heirship certificate (Warish Sanad) from the City Corporation / Union Parishad / Pourashava, naming all legal heirs.
  3. Collect the land documents: deeds, Khatian, tax receipts.
  4. Apply for mutation (Namjari) by inheritance, naming all heirs and their shares.
  5. Pay land development tax in the names of all heirs.

For banks, savings certificates or insurance, a Succession Certificate from the Civil Court may be needed.

Disputes usually arise when one heir takes control of the property. Typical problems include:

  • One heir sells the whole property or mutates it solely in his name.
  • Forged heirship certificates omitting heirs abroad.
  • Forged gift deeds or wills.
  • Occupation by a sibling without paying other heirs.

Remedies include an application for cancellation of mutation, a suit for declaration and partition (the Partition Act 1893), injunction and, where documents have been forged, a criminal complaint. Courts take time, so act as soon as you learn of a problem.

• Appoint a trusted advocate with a limited Power of Attorney to represent you.
  • Make sure your name, parents' names and NID/passport details match the heirship certificate.
  • Do not sign "no objection" or relinquishment papers without independent legal advice.
  • If you wish to give up your share, do it by a properly registered deed.
  • Keep proof of your relationship (birth certificate, NID, passport).

1. Obtain the heirship certificate with all heirs' names.
  2. Verify the current mutation and tax records.
  3. Get a deed search to ensure no transfer has been made without your consent.
  4. Reach a written, registered partition agreement if the family agrees.
  5. If not, file a partition suit with an injunction against sale.

faqs.question: Do heirs living abroad have inheritance rights in Bangladesh?
faqs.answer: Yes. Residence abroad does not reduce an heir's legal share under Muslim, Hindu or Christian succession law.

faqs.question: How much does a daughter get under Muslim law?
faqs.answer: A daughter receives half of a son's share when there are sons. A sole daughter gets 1/2 of the estate, and two or more daughters together get 2/3 if there are no sons.

faqs.question: How do I get an heirship certificate in Bangladesh?
faqs.answer: Apply to the Union Parishad, Pourashava or City Corporation with the death certificate, NIDs and family information. They issue a Warish Sanad naming the heirs.

faqs.question: Can a brother sell inherited property without my consent?
faqs.answer: He can only sell his own share. A sale of the entire property without co-heirs' consent can be challenged, and you can seek injunction and cancellation in court.

faqs.question: What if my siblings refuse to divide the property?
faqs.answer: You can file a partition suit in the Civil Court to have the property divided according to each heir's legal share.
